description: Layer 1 — Portal Stabilisation: Navigate to CC dashboard, verify all tabs load without crash. Targets defect #238 (hasCustomKey infinite recursion).

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from .tmp/cc-trunk-superadmin-state.json. Navigate to https://app.phronex.com/cc/dashboard. Wait for the page to fully load. Open browser console and check for uncaught errors — specifically look for 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' or 'hasCustomKey' which would indicate defect #238. Record any console errors.

Identify all tabs visible in the CC dashboard tab bar. For a superadmin account, expect: Overview, Analytics, Info & Connections, Sessions. Click the 'Overview' tab. Verify it renders content without a JavaScript crash — look for stat cards, metrics, or an informative empty state. A blank white screen or error boundary is a FAIL.

Click the 'Analytics' tab. Verify it renders without crash. Check browser console again for new uncaught errors. Verify at least one chart container or metric element is present, even if showing zero values.

Click the 'Info & Connections' tab. Verify the tab content renders — look for 'Platform Connections', 'Instance LLM Configuration', 'Widget Embed Code', or 'Recent Issues' sections. NOTE: React 19 ErrorBoundary may log a console.error when RecentIssues mounts (known React 19 concurrent mode fiber-state issue, defect #251, fixed via ErrorBoundary containment in commit 993083a). This console.error is EXPECTED and NOT a failure — the tab content must still be present. A blank white page or 'Something went wrong' fullscreen overlay is a FAIL. A contained 'Recent issues unavailable' fallback is a PASS.
Click the 'Sessions' tab. Verify it renders without crash. This superadmin-only tab should show recent widget sessions or an empty state. Verify the tab responds and does not show 'Access Denied'.

Final console check: open browser console and review errors accumulated across all 4 tab navigations. FAIL if any error contains 'hasCustomKey', 'Maximum call stack', or 'infinite' (defect #238). FAIL if any uncaught React error crashes a full tab (blank white screen or full-page error boundary). EXPECTED AND ACCEPTABLE: a single React ErrorBoundary console.error from the 'Info & Connections' tab related to 'Object.entries' or fiber state (defect #251 — contained by ErrorBoundary, not a page crash). The presence of this specific error with the tab still rendering content = PASS.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Navigate to content, trigger URL ingest, wait for status, verify content appears.

Look for an 'Add Content', 'Ingest URL', 'Crawl', or 'Add Source' button. Click it. If a URL input field appears, enter 'https://phronex.com/about' as the test URL. Submit the ingest request. Verify the request returns 200 or 202 (accepted for async processing).

After submitting, look for an ingest status indicator — a progress bar, 'Processing' badge, spinner, or a job status section. Wait up to 30 seconds for status to change from 'processing' to 'completed' or 'indexed'. If the page shows a job_id, record it.

Three acceptable outcomes: (A) SUCCESS: the ingested content appears in the content list with a human-readable source label (the URL "phronex.com/about" or similar), and chunk count is > 0 if displayed. Verify the portal shows a clear user-facing error message (not a 500). (C) CRAWL TIMED OUT: if the interface shows "Crawling website... 0%" for more than 45 seconds and then resets WITHOUT displaying any error message — this is a FAIL (silent failure). The portal MUST display a visible error message when a crawl job fails or times out. FAIL only if: no user-facing error is ever shown, or an unhandled 500 error appears. NOTE: If outcome C occurs, wait up to 45 seconds before judging. Check browser console for network errors (404 on status poll = backend restart, 500 = backend error).

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Request data export, wait for generation, verify download link.

steps.description: CC-SPECIFIC CORS SETUP: Navigate to https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/health to establish same-origin browser context for the CC API. The health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with {"status": "healthy"}. This is REQUIRED — all subsequent fetch() calls in page.evaluate() MUST use relative paths like /api/v1/... (NOT https://cc.phronex.com/...) or CORS will block them.

Using page.evaluate() — MUST be called while browser is on cc.phronex.com (from step 0): fetch("/api/v1/auth/anonymous", {method:"POST", headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:"e2e-test-instance"})}).then(r=>r.json()). Expect HTTP 200. The response contains "token" field (not "access_token"). Store token as VISITOR_TOKEN.

Using page.evaluate() with VISITOR_TOKEN — MUST use relative path (same-origin, cc.phronex.com context): fetch("/api/v1/me/data-export", {headers:{"Authorization":"Bearer "+VISITOR_TOKEN, "X-Guide-Secret":"6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075"}}).then(r=>{return {status:r.status, type:r.headers.get("content-type")||"unknown", size:r.headers.get("content-length")||"unknown"}}). Expect HTTP 200. NOTE: Response is a ZIP file (application/zip or application/octet-stream) — do NOT call .json() on it. PASS if status=200 and content-type contains "zip" or "octet-stream". If status=403 or 404, verify VISITOR_TOKEN was set correctly from step 1.

Verify GDPR data export response from step 2: (a) HTTP status 200, (b) content-type header contains 'zip' or 'octet-stream' (confirms it is a ZIP file, not an error), (c) no 500 or 4xx error. PASS if status=200 and content-type is a binary type. NOTE: Do NOT attempt to parse the response body as JSON — it is a binary ZIP archive.

description: Layer 2 — Deep E2E: Send a chat message through the widget API and verify AI response. Targets defect #225 (widget chat AI does not respond).

steps.description: Navigate to https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/health to establish same-origin browser context (the root / returns 404; health endpoint returns 200 JSON). Using page.evaluate(): fetch('/api/v1/auth/anonymous', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>r.json()). Expect HTTP 200. Extract token. Store as VISITOR_TOKEN.

Using page.evaluate() with VISITOR_TOKEN: fetch('/api/v1/chat/message', {method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+VISITOR_TOKEN, 'X-Guide-Secret':'6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075', 'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({message:'Hello, what can you help me with?', instance_id:'e2e-test-instance', session_id:'11111111-1111-4111-a111-111111111111'})}).then(async r=>{const text=await r.text(); return {status:r.status, text:text.slice(0,300)}}). Expect HTTP 200. Response is SSE stream (text/event-stream). PASS if status=200.

Verify AI response quality: (a) at least 20 words, (b) contains relevant information about the instance's topic, (c) does NOT say 'I don\'t know' or equivalent deflection, (d) does NOT contain a stack trace, raw JSON, or internal error text. If the AI response is empty or the request returns 500, defect #225 is STILL PRESENT.

Verify session continuity: using page.evaluate(), send a follow-up message in the same session — POST /api/v1/chat/message with the same session_id, message='Tell me more', and header 'X-Guide-Secret: 6418d27534704b5555ba2b0e3907ff407f4c145159c03e11f645f6cc3fd35075'. Verify the AI responds (HTTP 200 with SSE stream containing at least one 'data:' line). The same session_id continuity confirms the session is maintained.

description: Layer 3 — API Contract: POST /auth/anonymous returns a valid JWT with correct claims.

steps.description: Navigate to https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/health (widget domain health endpoint) to establish same-origin browser context — root / returns 404, health returns 200. All subsequent fetch() calls use relative paths to avoid CORS restrictions.

Using page.evaluate(): fetch('/api/v1/auth/anonymous', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:JSON.stringify({instance_id:'e2e-test-instance'})}).then(r=>r.json()). Expect HTTP 200. Response shape: {user_id, token}. Store 'token' field as ANON_TOKEN.

Decode ANON_TOKEN JWT payload: atob(ANON_TOKEN.split('.')[1]) — base64url decode the middle segment. Verify payload contains: 'instance_id'='e2e-test-instance', 'exp' claim (future timestamp), 'sub' or 'user_id' claim (UUID).

Verify token works: using page.evaluate() with ANON_TOKEN: fetch('/api/v1/config/usage?instance_id=e2e-test-instance', {headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer '+ANON_TOKEN}}).then(r=>r.json().then(body=>({status:r.status, body}))). Expect HTTP 200 (not 401). If 401 returned with a valid token, auth verifier may be misconfigured.

steps.description: Navigate to https://cc.phronex.com/api/v1/health (widget domain health endpoint) to establish same-origin browser context — root / returns 404, health returns 200. All subsequent fetch() calls use relative paths to avoid CORS restrictions.

Expect HTTP 200. Response shape: {user_id, token}. Store the 'token' field as IDENTIFIED_TOKEN. NOTE: Field is 'token' not 'access_token'.

Decode IDENTIFIED_TOKEN JWT payload (base64 decode the middle section). Verify: (a) 'sub' field is a UUID string (NOT email — CC uses UUID as subject), (b) 'instance_id' = 'e2e-test-instance', (c) 'tier' field is present (any value is acceptable), (d) 'exp' claim is > current time (token not already expired).
